RE: Formal Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Quinn Delgado
Member ID: W149862261
Reference Number: POC-5142E8878F-52764
Date of Denial Notice: 2026-08-07
Requested Service/CPT: Shoulder labral/instability repair, CPT 29806
Appeal Deadline: 2027-02-03 (within 180 days of notice, per the denial letter)

Dear Appeals & Grievances Committee,

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 29806 (arthroscopic shoulder capsulorrhaphy/labral and instability repair), communicated in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-07, Reference No. POC-5142E8878F-52764. The stated reason for denial was that "the requested procedure does not meet the plan's applicable medical necessity criteria." I am requesting reconsideration and reversal of this denial based on the clinical record summarized below, and I am also requesting that the plan identify and produce the specific medical-necessity criteria it applied to this request.

**1. Identification of the applicable policy and a request for the specific criteria relied upon**

Based on my own research, Security Health Plan delegates prior-authorization medical necessity review of shoulder surgery ("Joint Surgery") to eviCore by Evernorth, which applies its clinical guideline titled "CMM-315: Shoulder Surgery-Arthroscopic and Open Procedures," part of eviCore's "Comprehensive Musculoskeletal Management Guidelines." I was able to locate and review a public copy of this guideline (Version 1.0.2025, stated on its cover page as "Guidelines Effective July 1, 2025"), which contains a table of contents listing, among other sections, "Labral Repair" and "Arthroscopic or Open Surgical Procedures for Shoulder Instability and/or Laxity." I was not able to obtain the full operative text of those two specific sections — i.e., the actual numbered indications the plan or eviCore applied to CPT 29806 in Quinn Delgado's case. **I am not quoting or attributing any specific indication criteria for labral repair or instability repair to the plan, because I have not verified that language.**

Consistent with eviCore's own published process ("If you require a copy of the guidelines that were used to make a determination on a specific request of treatment or services, please email the case number and request to: reqcriteria@EviCore.com"), I am requesting that Security Health Plan and/or eviCore provide, in writing, the complete, dated text of the specific "Labral Repair" and/or "Shoulder Instability" criteria applied to Reference No. POC-5142E8878F-52764, so that the criteria can be addressed point-by-point. Please also confirm the exact guideline number, version, and effective date relied upon at the time of the determination.

**2. The clinical record supports medical necessity under the general framework of the applicable guideline**

The one general principle I was able to confirm directly from CMM-315 states: "The determination of medical necessity for the performance of shoulder surgery is always made on a case-by-case basis." The same document defines the diagnosis at issue as follows: a "Bankart Tear" is "a tear in the labrum located in the front, lower (anterior, inferior) part of the glenoid. This type of tear occurs most commonly during a shoulder dislocation and makes the shoulder more prone to recurrent dislocations," and "Shoulder Instability and/or Laxity" includes "Post-traumatic shoulder instability," defined as involving "an individual with a previous injury that has stretched or torn the ligaments of the shoulder." Quinn Delgado's case-specific record, summarized below, falls squarely within these definitions and, in our view (stated in our own words, since we could not verify the plan's specific numeric indications), meets the kind of clinical severity, imaging confirmation, and failed conservative care that such guidelines are designed to identify as appropriate for surgery:

- **Duration and pattern of instability:** Nine months of recurrent episodes of shoulder instability with apprehension, including three anterior dislocations, the most recent requiring reduction in the emergency department.
- **Imaging confirmation:** MR arthrogram of the shoulder dated 2026-06-25 demonstrates an anteroinferior labral tear (Bankart lesion) with a small Hill-Sachs lesion and glenoid bone loss under 10%; the rotator cuff is intact. This is the precise pathology the guideline's own definition of "Bankart Tear" describes as making "the shoulder more prone to recurrent dislocations."
- **Physical examination:** Positive apprehension and relocation tests and increased anterior translation on load-and-shift testing, with full strength — objective findings of structural instability, not simply pain.
- **Failed conservative management:** A full course of supervised physical therapy focused on rotator cuff and scapular stabilizer strengthening with activity modification — 24 visits over 10 weeks (2026-04-05 to 2026-06-14), as documented in the physical therapy discharge note — plus four months of NSAID use during flares. Injection therapy was not pursued because it is not an appropriate or indicated treatment for structural instability. This represents a complete, guideline-consistent trial of non-surgical management, not merely a token attempt.
- **Functional impact:** Quinn Delgado avoids overhead reaching and cannot return to work duties requiring lifting because of the instability.
- **No contraindications to surgery:** No active infection, no untreated substance use disorder, BMI 29, non-smoker — there is no medical reason to further delay definitive treatment.

**3. Request**

For the reasons above, I respectfully request that Security Health Plan reverse the denial of CPT 29806 and authorize the requested labral/instability repair. In the alternative, I request:
(a) written identification of the specific CMM-315 (or other) criteria applied to this determination, including guideline number, version, and effective date;
(b) a peer-to-peer review between Security Health Plan's/eviCore's reviewing physician and Dr. Marchetti; and
(c) confirmation of receipt of this appeal and of the applicable internal appeal decision timeframe.

This appeal is submitted well within the 180-day deadline stated in the denial notice (by 2027-02-03).

Enclosed/attached in support of this appeal:
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-04-05 to 2026-06-14, 24 visits)
- MR arthrogram report dated 2026-06-25
- Office visit/exam notes documenting apprehension and relocation test findings, load-and-shift testing, and strength exam
- Emergency department record of the most recent dislocation/reduction
- Letter of medical necessity from Dr. Marchetti, orthopedic surgery
- Copy of the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-07 (Ref. POC-5142E8878F-52764)

Please direct all correspondence regarding this appeal to me at the address and phone number below, with a copy to Dr. Marchetti's office.
